newsitem.title: JAPAN: S&P to assign 'pi' ratings to more Japanese banks.
newsitem.headline: S&P to assign 'pi' ratings to more Japanese banks.

text.p: Standard & Poor's (S&P) said on Tuesday it would assign public information (pi) ratings to more Japanese banks, including some of the nation's 20 biggest banks and second-tier regional banks, in the future.

Ernest Napier, a director at S&P, told reporters the international rating agency would assign its "pi" ratings to larger financial institutions in the first half of the coming year. He also said it would assign pi ratings to at least one second-tier regional bank in January and to more second-tier regional banks in the next few months.

S&P earlier said it had assigned pi ratings to seven Japanese regional banks. These are unsolicited debt ratings based on information available to the public rather than lengthy consultations with the issuer. They are differentiated from other ratings by the letters pi after the rating.

S&P assigned an Api rating to Hachijuni Bank Ltd, BBBpi ratings to five regional banks, and a BBpi rating to Kiyo Bank Ltd. The five regional banks rated BBBpi are Bank of Yokohama Ltd, Hyakujushi Bank Ltd, Iyo Bank Ltd, Nanto Bank Ltd and Suruga Bank Ltd.
"This is only the beginning," Napier said.

S&P said it had divided "pi" ratings into 10 stages because of a strong preference among counterparties and other market participants for its "AAA" through "D" scale, which is globally recognised as a benchmark for financial risk.
Ratings in the "AAA", "AA", "A" and "BBB" categories are regarded as investment grade, while the "BB" category is regarded as having speculative characteristics.

The rating agency assigned "BBpi" ratings to Kiyo Bank as the bank had poor asset quality that continued to negatively affect earnings and the bank's financial flexibility, said Naoko Nemoto, an associate director at S&P.
She said Kiyo Bank's capital adequacy was weak, especially given the high level of problem loans compared with most first-tier regional banks and the expectation of future loan losses.

S&P currently assigns traditional credit ratings to nine nationwide commercial banks, two long-term credit banks and Norinchukin Bank. It also assigns traditional credit ratings to six trust banks and seven regional banks.
Among Japan's 13 biggest nationwide commercial and long-term credit banks, Hokkaido Takushoku Bank Ltd and Nippon Credit Bank Ltd do not currently request ratings from S&P.
